Commentary.Commentary: We are back. The Pakistan players are in a huddle near the ropes before they disperse. They are joined by the two Dutch openers. Vikramjit Singh and Max O'Dowd will open the innings for the Netherlands. Shaheen Afridi is at the top of his mark and is raring to go. Two slips in place. Let's play...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, the match is evenly poised at the halfway mark. It should get easier to bat under lights but Pakistan have the resources to defend the total. No team has ever chased a 280-plus score against Pakistan in ODI World Cups. Can the Dutch batters rise to the challenge? We shall find out when we return for the chase.

Roelof van der Merwe is in for a chat. He says that they executed their plans well and kept Pakistan under pressure with their fielding throughout. Praises Aryan Dutt for his opening spell. Mentions that there are always going to be partnerships under the lights as it gets a bit easier to bat on. Says that a good start should do it for them. Ends by saying that you get a bit grumpier as you get old but he is happy with the performance from him as well as the team.

After being asked to bat by Scott Edwards, Pakistan were off to a nervy start in their batting effort. Fakhar Zaman departed cheaply yet again and the departure of Imam-ul-Haq and Babar Azam in the space of 5 deliveries sent the cat among pigeons early. Mohammad Rizwan and Saud Shakeel then joined hands and began resurrecting the innings with a positive intent. Thanks to a 120-run stand between these two, Pakistan began to breathe again. After the wicket of Shakeel, Pakistan started to lose their way and it looked like they would get rolled over quickly. However, Mohammad Nawaz and Shadab Khan had other plans as they got together and kept the scoreboard ticking. Their dismissals pegged Pakistan back again before a 19-run stand for the last wicket took them over 280.

A job well done by the Netherlands to bowl Pakistan out for 286! The Netherlands opted to start with the off spin of Aryan Dutt from one end and although it did not fetch them a wicket, he managed to keep the batters in check. Logan van Beek was equally good from the other end and even dealt an early blow. His fellow pacer Paul van Meekeren struck with his first delivery to remove the other opener before an inspired bowling change in the form of Colin Ackermann got the big wicket of Babar Azam. In the middle phase, they were stalled by the gritty stand between Shakeel and Rizwan. The Netherlands came roaring back with two quick wickets but were unable to run through the Pakistan lower order. They did pull it back but Scott Edwards will feel that Pakistan have got more runs than they should have. Bas de Leede was the star of the show with figures of 4 for 62 from his nine overs.

OUT! STUMPED! A fantastic piece of glove work from Scott Edwards! That is it for Pakistan then. Colin Ackermann sees the batter advance down the track and fires this one full and outside off, Haris Rauf is way out of his crease and tries to reach it but fails to do so, Scott Edwards collects it and shows quick reflexes to dive to his left to break the stumps with Rauf well outside the crease. The replay confirms it and Pakistan have been bowled out for 286.

Babar Azam, the captain of Pakistan says that reception in India has been really good and they are looking after us well. Adds that everyone is enjoying their time and they believe in their openers Imam-ul-Haq and Fakhar Zaman while Haris Rauf, Shaheen Afridi, and Hasan Ali are the pacers for this game. Reckons a score of 290-300 runs will be good on this wicket.

The skipper of the Netherlands, Scott Edwards says that they will bowl first. Adds that it is a pretty good wicket and hold together throughout the game. Mentions that it will be easier to bat under lights. Shares that they have played a lot against Pakistan and are looking forward to another close clash. Feels that it will be about adjusting and seeing what the pitch does. Ends by saying that they have quality pacers and spinners.
TOSS - The coin lands in favour of Scott Edwards and Netherlands have elected to BOWL first.
